facts.statement: The genus was described by Hua and Jouve in 2004, and the type species A. krebsi honors Bernard Krebs.
facts.quote: Described by Hua and Jouve in 2004, the type species is A. krebsi, with the species named for Bernard Krebs.

facts.statement: Argochampsa lived in Morocco during the Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: It lived in the Paleocene of Morocco.

facts.statement: The animal possessed a long, narrow snout and likely lived a marine lifestyle.
facts.quote: Argochampsa had a long narrow snout, and appears to have been marine in habits.

facts.statement: The genus is based on a nearly complete skull (OCP DEK-GE 1201) found in the Oulad Abdoun Basin near Khouribga, Morocco.
facts.quote: Argochampsa is based on OCP DEK-GE 1201, a nearly complete skull from the Oulad Abdoun Basin, in the vicinity of Khouribga, Morocco.

facts.statement: The skull measured 43.3 centimeters in length, with the snout comprising approximately 70% of the total skull length.
facts.quote: The skull, 43.3 centimeters long (17.0 in), had a long, narrow snout, marking it as a longirostrine crocodilian; the snout made up about 70% of the skull's length.

facts.statement: The upper jaw contained five teeth in each premaxilla and 26 teeth in each maxilla.
facts.quote: There were five teeth in each premaxilla and 26 in each maxilla (the main tooth-bearing bone of the upper jaw).

facts.statement: Concave depressions on the lacrimal and prefrontal bones indicate the presence of salt glands.
facts.quote: Argochampsa had concave depressions on the internal surface of the lacrimal and prefrontal bones, indicating the presence of salt glands.

facts.statement: Additional fossils recovered include the lower jaw, neck and back vertebrae, upper arm, and armor.
facts.quote: More recently, material from the lower jaw, neck and back vertebrae, the upper arm, and armor has been recovered.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Argochampsa under the parent group Gavialidae.
The time range for Argochampsa spans from the Danian to the Ypresian, between 66 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Ypresian (66 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Argochampsa is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodylomorph usually classified as a gavialoid related to modern gharials.
rejected.quote: Argochampsa (meaning "Argo crocodile", in reference to the mythological Argo of Jason) is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodylomorph, usually regarded as a gavialoid crocodilian, related to modern gharials.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodylomorph usually'

rejected.statement: Lee and Yates (2018) debated that Argochampsa was likely not a gavialoid or crocodylian, but a non-crocodylian eusuchian.
rejected.quote: Lee & Yates (2018) considered it most likely that Argochampsa was not a gavialoid, or even a crocodylian, but rather a member of the clade of non-crocodylian eusuchians.
